title: Playing with Art Tatum and his blindness
summary: Roy took Tatum to the Rhythm Club, they jammed at the Devil's Kitchen, and Roy doubts Tatum was totally blind.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Art Tatum: the legend, the piano and the man

blocks.x: When Art first came here... I think I was working at Small's, yeah... Me and Joe carried him down to the Rhythm Club, and we played... We played about two tunes before we cut him loose. And I'll never forget, Fats was playing pool, and Fletcher and all the cats were playing cards and shit. And we was playing something, and all of a sudden, boom, we all dropped out. Boy, you could hear a rat piss on cotton, because that (?) tore that Rhythm Club up, you know.

He used to pick me up every night, you know, and we'd go to these different jobs. We used to go to one joint... He's supposed to be blind, right? Shit. It was called... The Devil's Kitchen, I think it was, or something like that. It was across Fifth Avenue... Across Lenox, between Lenox

and Fifth, down in the cellar, you know. The piano had very few keys on it. But he could play it. I try and laugh at these cats who always talk about, "Well, we finally got a decent piano." He played any of them pianos, ones that had four keys on it!

So we'd go down there and we'd play, because we did a lot of playing in those days. And maybe a chick would ask him for a number, you know. Then that's when he really went to his blind bit, you know. He'd start reaching for his beer. "Oh, honey, I'll give it to you," you know, and he'd take it. I said, "Why don't you stop jivin', man!"
He was a lot of fun. We had a lot of good times together, man.
You told me once that he could see well that he was quite a card player.

Yeah, he played cards! But I'm telling you, going to that place, you would have trouble getting in that place without stumbling, you know. In other words, he wasn't... I don't think he was totally blind.
He had I think what they call peripheral vision. At a certain angle he'd be able to see. Something similar to what Brooks Kerr had before he went completely blind.
I didn't know that. Well, I don't know...
